The captioned group of Appeals are filed by the State, under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 read with Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure,1908, challenging the common judgment and award dated 22.02.2022, passed by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge, Modasa,
Dist: Aravalli, in Land Reference Case Nos.1 to 4 of 2021 of Village:Jhalodar, Taluka:Modasa,
whereby the learned Court had valued the land at the rate of Rs.1910/- per square meter for agricultural land and Rs.2484/- per Square Meter for non- agricultural land.

entities.text: Land Reference Case Nos.1 to 4 of 2021

sentences.text:
3. Learned Assistant Government Pleader Ms.Tanushree Shrimal would seek to challenge the said judgment on various grounds and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2790/2023 ORDER DATED:
17/07/2023 undefined whereas, it would appear that the issue in question may not be res-integra,
more particularly, the issue in question as submitted by learned Advocate Mr.Jani, on behalf of the respondents-claimants, would stand covered by a decision of an Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court dated 11.11.2022, in First Appeal No. 2210 of 2022 and allied matters.

4. It appears that the decision of this Court in First Appeal No.2210 of 2022 was concerning a group of First Appeals more particularly, Land Reference Cases Nos.123 to 133 of 2017, 135, 137 to 139 of 2017 and 141, 142, 144 to 150 of 2017, as noted at paragraph No.2.5 of the judgment, more particularly, the said land references related to village Gajan, which according to learned advocate Mr.Jani is an adjacent village and therefore being a NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2790/2023 ORDER DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined comparable instance and whereas, under such circumstances according to learned Advocate the said decision would cover the present issue also.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 5. Learned Advocate Mr.Jani would submit that the land in question had been acquired for the purpose of constructing a four lane State Highway connecting Shmalaji- Modasa- Malpur- Lunawada - Godhra - Halol.

Learned Advocate would submit, that the notifications under Section 4,
with regard to the present village i.e village:Jhalodar, Taluka:Modasa was issued on 26.03.2010,whereas, notification under Section 6, in the case of village Jhalodar was issued on 25.06.2010 whereas the notification in case of the references in case of village Gajan was issued on 20.08.2008.

5.1. Learned Advocate would submit that award NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2790/2023 ORDER DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined under Section 11 was issued near about the same time, i.e while the award for the village Jhalodar was issued on 11.03.2011.
The land at village Jhalodar was valued at Rs.12.50/- per Square Meter.

2 5.2.

sentences.text: Learned Advocate would submit as noted herein above that the agriculture land was valued by the Reference Court in the present case at the rate of Rs.1910/- per square meter for agricultural land and Rs.2484/- per Square Meter for non-agricultural land whereas, in the comparable case for village Gajan it was valued by the Learned Reference Court at Rs.1925/- per sq mtr., and non-agricultural land was valued at Rs.2002/- for village Umedpur, whereas, in the comparable case, non- agricultural land was valued at Rs.2503/- per sq.mtr..
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2790/2023 ORDER DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined 5.3.

Learned Advocate would submit that all the aspects almost remain the same and though the notification under Section 4 in the comparable instance was 3 years prior to the notification in the present case,
yet higher compensation was awarded in case of the said land, though according to Learned advocate as it appeared on record the land of the village:Jhalodar may have higher potentiality than the land of the comparable instance i.e village Gajan.
5.4.

Learned Advocate would submit that in the case of the said land since Hon'ble Division Bench had rejected the First Appeals, holding that no error has been committed by the learned Reference Court, the same proposition may be made applicable here.

5.5. Learned Advocate would submit that since NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2790/2023 ORDER DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined both the land are falling on the same Highway for the purpose of which the land had been acquired and whereas, since there is no other discernible difference between both the land, therefore, the impugned judgment and award issued by Learned Reference Court may be confirmed by this Court.

6. From a perusal of the judgment of the Hon'ble Division Bench, more particularly, in reference to the facts as noted herein above, with regard to the notification under Section 4 and 6 and award under Section 11, it appears that there may not be any difference regard to the potentiality of the land situated at Village Gajan i.e the comparable instance and Village Jhalodar.

7. It also requires to be noted that learned Reference Court had determined the market NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2790/2023 ORDER DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined value of the land at village Jhalodar, relying upon a comparable instance i.e an adjoining village Saira.

The Hon'ble Division Bench having examined the record has come to a conclusion that the reference Court did not commit any error whatsoever, in holding that village Saira was a comparable instance and thus the market value of the land acquired in Village Gajan could be calculated taking the market value of the land at Village Saira as a comparable instance.

8. In the instant case from the map, more particularly, a screenshot from Google Map, which is tendered by learned Advocate for the respondent, it appears that Village Gajan and Village Jhalodar are on the same Highway.

9. The learned Reference Court has also relied on award for village Gajan which is at NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2790/2023 ORDER DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined distance of 4.37 kms and therefore has rightly reduced compensation by 20% from the award of 2017 which was confirmed in The State Of Gujarat vs Patel Shankarbhai Maganbhai on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53298642/

sentences.text:
10. In view of the above, more particularly, since it appears that land situated at Village Gajan, were acquired for the very same purpose and whereas, since it also appears that the same was taken as comparable instance, more particularly, the present land may be having more potentiality than village Gajan and also having regard to the fact that the appeals against judgments of the land reference Court as regards to village Gajan have been rejected by the Division Bench of this Court,
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2790/2023 ORDER DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined therefore, in the considered opinion of this Court, no case for admission of the present appeals is made out.
11.
Hence, in view of the above discussion, the present appeals are hereby dismissed.
Judgment and award passed by the learned reference Court in all the First appeals are hereby confirmed.

The compensation along with consequential statutory benefits accrued till date to the claimants shall be deposited within a period of eight weeks from the receipt of copy of this order with the reference Court by the State Government.
Consequentially, all the allied civil applications stand disposed of.

(BHARGAV D. KARIA, J) PALAK The State Of Gujarat vs Patel Shankarbhai Maganbhai on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53298642/
